rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claims 116 and 093 (with claim 068): the address record's field shape is the address book service's design and transporter records follow the real services, which keep transporters in their own records; the germinal data fields page, which outranks the prototype on data, never says the '**' row applies to every address (claim 077) and draws the whole block from one transporter (claim 102-m1), so it does not contradict the next-ranked sources, the prototype (address form asks no authorisation number; the commercial transporter page asks it) and the address book record (no such field), which agree and settle it.
outcome: Only transporters carry a transporter authorisation number. Address-book addresses (origin or consignor, destination, consignee or importer, and branch) get no transporter authorisation number and the address form asks none; commercial transporters, added through their own pages, keep the authorisation number (text, at most 255 characters, such as UK/CARMA/T2/00107003) those pages ask for. The germinal page's '**' marks a transporter-only row: its examples all describe one transport company, the address record's field shape is the address book service's design (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 116), and transporter records follow the real services (claim 093).
